# Family crossing: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `family-cross.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.39) and `family-cross-rules.soar` (23 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`; `tools/rosie_river.py`). Needs Soar 9.6.6.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . family-cross.soar --seed 1 --cap 300000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . family-cross.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py family-cross init-familycross.world

`python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with another example state as the initial world.

World: init-familycross.world (two banks; two adults, two children and the boat on the first bank).

## Results (Soar 9.6.6, 16 Nov 2026)

Plans were replayed independently by `check_plan.py` (legality from the action statements, the losing conditions, the goal).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`) | final-familycross: goal true, failure false; init-familycross: goal false, failure false. All as the instructor intended. |
| Seeds 1-3, library v2.39 | solved: 9 crossings on every seed (the instructor's "nine steps", the shortest), 3,461 / 3,767 / 3,644 decisions |
| Seed 1, library v2.37, no control on real moves | solved: 9 crossings, 5,194 decisions |

## Translation

- Operators: ferry-one ("the boat and a block on the current bank onto the opposite bank"; argument1 = the block, argument2 = the opposite bank) and ferry-two-children (statement 4, not named in the dialog: "a child ... and another child ... and the boat"; argument1 and argument2 = the two blocks, the lower ^index first; the destination is the opposite bank). Each operator records the bank it leaves (^from), so its look-ahead application fires once.
- current is expanded in place (a bank below the boat); opposite is a maintained one-argument relation.
- The goal ("all the blocks are on a destination bank") is expanded over the blocks of the world file (the boat is a block).
- No losing condition is taught. "The solution has nine steps." is checked against the plans, not used.
- Search control added at JL's direction (16 Nov 2026), not from the English: in look-ahead, a move whose result is a situation already on the current look-ahead path is rejected. A situation is the bank of every block; each operator carries the label of the situation it produces (^result), the task object the label of the current one (^situation), and the look-ahead application records both on the history object (^visited). Real moves (JL, 16 Nov 2026, as in mc-world): a real move back to a situation already visited is worst (the top state records ^real-visited).

## Assumption ledger

| ID | Statements | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| A-FC1 | 4 | The two-child action has no name in the dialog; it is called `ferry-two-children`. |
| A-FC2 | 4, 8 | "the boat and a block" / "the boat": the blocks named are not the boat; the boat always moves. |
| A-C1 | all | "all the blocks" is expanded over the blocks of the world file (the boat is a block), so the goal test is positive. |
| A-C2 | all | "current" is expanded in place; "opposite" tests absence and decides legality, so it is a maintained one-argument relation. |
| A-C3 | all | "The solution has N steps." is checked against the plans, not used. |
| S-1 | (JL) | Search control, not from the English (16 Nov 2026): in look-ahead, a move whose result is a situation already on the look-ahead path is rejected. |
| S-2 | (JL) | Search control, not from the English (16 Nov 2026, as in Tasks/From-English/mc-world): a real move back to a situation already visited is worst. |
